newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-RBA says concerned about future AWOTE growth.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-RBA says concerned about future AWOTE growth.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of Australia said in its quarterly Bulletin that average weekly ordinary time earnings (AWOTE) are currently consistent with the RBA's inflation objective, but that it was concerned about future wage outcomes.

"While AWOTE is currently consistent with the 2-3 percent inflation objective, this reflects the modest growth in employment of the past year: the forward looking concern is that with employment growing more strongly, AWOTE would once again be running at a pace which threatens price stability," the bank said.
The RBA said the slowing in economy-wide measures of wages seemed largely to reflect the cyclical fall in employment.
"New settlements are yet to show evidence of slowing," the bank said.
"The result of continuing high settlements in new enterprise agreements is that average wage rises contained in all currently active agreements have been rising," the bank said.

"Moderation might yet become apparent although the transition to a more deregulated labour market poses the risk that efforts to restore traditional wage relativities might also raise aggregate wages growth," it said.
However, the bank said prospective low rates of inflation should be conducive to a greater of wages restraint.

Average weekly ordinary time earnings for adults employed full time rose 1.3 percent in the three months to May for an annual rise of 3.9, while private sector average weekly ordinary time earnings rose 1.2 percent in the three months for a rise of 4.4 percent.
The Reserve Bank has previously expressed concern that the level of annual wage increases should not exceed 4.5 percent to avoid threatening low inflation.
